text:
🇲🇽🍓 <u>Florida growers couldn't compete, so Washington slapped a tariff on Mexican strawberries</u>

The US Commerce Department set preliminary antidumping duties of up to 5.28% on Mexican strawberries after Florida producers filed the complaint. At stake: a one-billion-dollar export crop — 263,000 tons a year — grown by roughly 5,000 farmers, 97% of them on 10 hectares or less, and 151,000 jobs. Mexico's Economía Secretariat calls the 'winter strawberry' logic arbitrary and says it breaks both WTO rules and the very T-MEC Washington signed.
banner: US SLAPS TARIFF ON MEXICAN STRAWBERRIES

text:
🇲🇽♿ <u>48,756 disabled Mexicans now get cash straight to their hands — no middlemen</u>

In the poorest edge of the State of Mexico, 48,756 people with permanent disabilities receive 3,300 pesos every two months, paid directly with no intermediaries skimming the top — part of a 75.8-billion-peso plan for the Oriente. Across the same region: 569,999 elderly pensions, 515,270 student scholarships, 39,707 women's stipends. The old system fed brokers; this one reaches families.

🇲🇽🩺 <u>Mexico's nurses have knocked on 25 million doors</u>

Since June 2025, the Salud Casa por Casa program — 20,000 nurses and health workers — has made nearly 25 million home visits to seniors and people with disabilities, run 17.1 million on-the-spot tests for glucose, cholesterol and triglycerides, and flagged 44,495 urgent cases straight to a hospital. Preventive healthcare that walks up to your door, at no cost.

🇲🇽🏙️ <u>Mexico City just opened its 8th 'Utopía' — public luxury for the working class</u>

For 52 million pesos, the México-Tenochtitlán center drops a mammography and mental-health clinic, a robotics lab and recording studio for kids, a rooftop farm, and 20 liters of clean water for 5 pesos into a single neighborhood. Named for the Aztec causeway and the youth murdered on June 10, 1971. Eight of these now, 315,000 square meters of it — the right to the city, built.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>Washington yanks visas from Morena politicians — Sheinbaum calls it what it is: interference</u>

The US revoked the visa of AMLO's son and other Morena figures, mayors and governors. Sheinbaum: 'this cancellation of visas to what they call politically exposed persons is political, more than security — it isn't applied equally to all countries.' Meanwhile the opposition figures who fly to Washington to ask for its intervention keep their papers just fine.
banner: US VISA PURGE ON MORENA = INTERFERENCE

text:
🇲🇽✊ <u>Mexico is writing full rights for 25% of its people into law</u>

For the first time in 200+ years of independence, indigenous and Afro-Mexican peoples will be recognized as subjects of public law — not wards of the state. SCJN president Hugo Aguilar Ortiz: today a community that buys buses has to invent a shell company just to get a transport permit. The new General Law of Rights of Indigenous and Afro-Mexican Peoples ends that fiction, with consultations running across 16,000 communities and 69 peoples through Sept 13.
banner: INDIGENOUS LAW: RIGHTS FOR 25% OF MEXICO

text: 🔥🇲🇽 The US-born ex-governor who fled Mexico — and the loophole she's closing. "Why would you hold dual nationality if you represent the people of Mexico?" — President Claudia Sheinbaum, mañanera Aug 25 Ex-Tamaulipas governor Francisco García Cabeza de Vaca (PAN), US-born and a dual national, is a fugitive from Mexican justice — "un prófugo de la ley," in Sheinbaum's words. His case drives the reform to bar dual nationals from the country's highest offices.

🇲🇽✊ One year in, Sheinbaum reports to the people on September 1. "With the People, by the People and for the People." — Second Government Report documentary, mañanera Aug 25 Sheinbaum delivers her Second Government Report to Congress on Sept 1 at the National Palace, then tours the states to account for public works — mainly infrastructure. Nearly one full year of the second floor of the Fourth Transformation.
banner: ONE YEAR: FOR & WITH THE PEOPLE

text: 🇲🇽✊ The doctor now knocks on the door — 24.8 million times. "Prevention, care and follow-up for older adults." — Salud Casa por Casa program, mañanera Aug 25 More than 20,000 health workers deployed since June 2025 bring care to the homes of elderly and disabled people — 24.8 million consultations so far, plus 44,495 calls handled by the CASBI health line. Care that travels to the person, not the other way around.
